answer: Like boats bidding for a limited number of berths at a crowded wharf, the economy auctions a fixed count of reward licenses each epoch. Identities are free; licenses are not. A sybil operator buying N slots just bids against itself, driving its own clearing price toward the full reward value, so the farm donates its profits back to the treasury that pays them. Honest agents compete once on the open meadow of the market. And like water dissolving karst, the public auction ledger dissolves any farm's secrecy: scaling stops being profit and becomes self-taxation.
